Alert.description: A risk or status alert on an entity.

AlertEntry.description: A regulatory-risk, reputational, or status alert on the entity.

type.description:
Alert categories. Native (MongoDB-sourced) alerts carry a lowercase category. Possible values:
- closed: deceased individuals; for organizations, liquidation, dissolution, cancellation, or deletion.
- regulatory: regulatory-risk alerts (criminal charges, arrests, legal proceedings, reputation-risk exposure).
- highprofile: wealth-ranking, notable-entrepreneur, top-taxpayer, or high-profit indicators (no regulatory implication; may be omitted).
- pep: politically exposed person.
- importantobg: leaks originating from diverse sources (may be omitted depending on use case).
- restriction: significant regulatory, legal, and business restrictions and risks.
- entityInfo: important information about the entity.
- systemic: organizations designated as systemically important for a state.
- strategic: organizations designated as strategically important for a state.
- listed: companies listed on stock exchanges.
- hidden: internal-logic alerts — must be ignored.
- disputedterritory: entities with addresses in disputed territories (may be excluded).
- sanctionterritory: entities from sanction-sensitive areas.
- other: deprecated alerts.

Autogenerated alerts — propagated across the graph from a flagged related entity, never native to
this entity — carry the propagated category in upper case: PEP_RELATED, SANCTION_RELATED,
HIGH_PROFILE_RELATED, SYSTEMIC_RELATED, STRATEGIC_RELATED, SANCTION_TERRITORY_RELATED,
LISTED_RELATED, STATECO_RELATED, RESTRICTION_RELATED, REP_RELATED. The case distinguishes the two
families; the category is the same token the graph and political-profile surfaces emit.

CorporateCategory.description:
A corporate relation category to request. Values:
- shareholdingInformation: shareholders of the analyzed entity (for organizations: shareholders, indirect shareholders, beneficial owners, participants; empty for persons).
- ownershipInOtherEntities: entities owned or controlled by the requested entity (organizations: subsidiaries and branches; persons: owned/controlled entities and minor shareholdings).
- executiveSenior: management-board members (organizations) / management-board or other high-ranking roles held (persons).
- board: board of directors and equivalents (organizations) / supervisory-board memberships (persons).
- executive: executive roles such as department heads or secretaries (organizations) / executive positions held (persons).
- political: public-administration roles such as members of parliament (organizations) / public-capacity roles held (persons).
- signature: individuals with signature rights (organizations) / signature rights held (persons).
- thirdParty: third-party service providers such as auditors and liquidators (organizations) / organizations served (persons).
- membership: membership affiliations.
Note: executive, executiveSenior, political, and board are not always precise across jurisdictions (the same term can differ by region) — request all categories to be safe.

get.summary: Resolve a PID to its members
get.description: Accepts ANY PID (entity or hub). An entity PID resolves to itself as a single member; a hub PID resolves to its group members. 200 with a status field for active/merged/never-minted: a merged PID follows its redirect to the live winner, a never-minted PID returns an empty list. An unmapped (dissolved) hub returns 410 GONE with a 'references' list — each former member with its resolvable entity PID and its current hub (or null if no longer grouped). A non-PID shape returns 400.

parameters.description: A PID (a 1-char type prefix P/O/U + 32 hex), as previously returned to the client.
parameters.name: pid
